answer: Yes, a meteg is printed. Host letter: alef (first letter of אתה), with the vowel qamats. Presence: high. Host alef: high. Vowel qamats: high.
visible_evidence: The whole word אתה and the points below it are clearly visible, with no ink from neighbouring lines touching them. Three separate marks sit below the line. Under the alef (right) is a qamats, a T-shaped mark. Just to the left of that qamats is a separate short vertical stroke with no crossbar. It sits at the alef's lower left, where the alef meets the tav, and is apart from the tav's own mark. Under the tav is a second qamats, also T-shaped (the tav's dagesh dot can be seen inside the letter). The ה has nothing under it. The lone vertical stroke is not part of either qamats, because each qamats has its own crossbar and stem. It is not a sheva either, since there are no dots. Its position, directly left of the alef's vowel, is where a meteg goes.
